text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel the wrist and hand pain, when it started, and what specific movements make it worse.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The patient's history of thumb and wrist pain radiating to the elbow, worsened by holding her infant (a classic aggravating factor for de Quervain's), and her age/sex demographic are highly suggestive. While her mother's history of joint pain treated with methotrexate raises a slight suspicion for inflammatory arthritis, the acute mechanical nature of her symptoms points more strongly to overuse tenosynovitis. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other pathologies, I will request a specific physical exam test.

REQUEST TEST: Finkelstein's Test
